summary: When the hero pushes a boulder onto a rolling-boulder trap, hack.c:moverock_core computes the trap launch endpoint and calls trap.c:launch_obj so the boulder rolls onward into the Sokoban pit. The JavaScript moverock_core emits the roll message and feels the trap, then records trap.c launch_obj as unported and returns without launching the boulder. The missing caller causes the first screen/RNG divergence at step 567; obj_resists is the next C RNG attribution after the omitted launched-object path.

source.branch: The hero pushes a boulder into a ROLLING_BOULDER_TRAP after ordinary pushability, monster, door and Sokoban diagonal checks. The source finds the launch endpoint, prints the roll message, feels the trap, launches the boulder with ROLL|LAUNCH_KNOWN, then returns whether another boulder remains at the source square.
callers: hack.c:moverock calls moverock_core for the square immediately ahead, then moverock_done; test_move reaches this path before domove_core completes the move.

js/hack.js:moverock calls moverock_core and the movement path invokes moverock; the JavaScript ROLLING_BOULDER_TRAP arm currently stops at note_unported instead of calling the existing trap_effects launch_obj rolling path.
dependencies: trap.c:launch_obj already has a JavaScript implementation in js/trap_effects.js for this rolling boulder path; it is private to trap_effects.js and needs an export to wire the hack.c caller.
The caller discards launch_obj’s integer return value, matching C; moverock_core uses sobj_at at the source square for its own return result.

evidence: challenges/manifests/v62.json identifies the case mission as hack.c:moverock ROLLING_BOULDER_TRAP launch_obj caller and sourcePointers as hack.c:moverock_core lines 594-614 -> trap.c:launch_obj with ROLL|LAUNCH_KNOWN.

Read upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/hack.c:moverock_core (348-638), especially the ROLLING_BOULDER_TRAP arm (594-614): C finds the launch endpoint, prints the roll message, calls feeltrap, then launches BOULDER from (sx,sy) to (tox,toy) and returns whether a boulder remains at the original square.

js/hack.js:moverock_core has the corresponding rolling-trap branch at lines 2609-2627; after the message and feeltrap it calls note_unported('trap.c launch_obj') and returns. The required trap_effects.js launch_obj helper already handles rolling boulder paths and is called by trap_effects.js trap activation code.

The saved v62 evaluation records 567/617 screens and the selected-base scan at 4c4706b0eb8d0d7b493816d203e56579af569f26 reproduces the mismatch at step 567: C reports the boulder rolling away and falling, while the JS screen still omits the resulting boulder state. C’s next recorded RNG is rn2(100)=99 in zap.c:obj_resists; JavaScript instead records rn2(19)=14. The actual missing behavior is the earlier moverock launch_obj caller, as identified independently by the v62 manifest source trace.

Implementation scope is hack.c:moverock_core plus the JS caller wiring/export needed for its existing trap.c:launch_obj callee; this differs from B’s reserved hack.c:domove_core and zap.c:zap_map scopes.
